# sta310r

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/eribul/sta310r/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/eribul/sta310r/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Package documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-eribul.github.io%2Fsta310r-blue)](https://eribul.github.io/sta310r/)
<!-- badges: end -->

`sta310r` collects the data sets that accompany Collett (2023), *Modelling
Survival Data in Medical Research* (4th edition), together with the computer
exercises used in the STA310 course at the University of Gothenburg. The package
focuses on the data sets, their documentation and the exercise vignettes.

## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pak::pak("eribul/sta310r")
```

## Name conflicts

The package includes six data sets with names also used by the `survival` package, for data
sets that are not the same:

- `bladder`
- `cgd`
- `kidney`
- `myeloma`
- `ovarian`
- `rats` 

Attach `sta310r` last (`library(sta310r)` AFTER `library(survival)`), or use `sta310r::xxx` explicitly if both packages are attached. You may also just refer to the datasets by their aliases as described below.

## Data sets by example

Each data set that is used in a worked example of Collett (2023) has an alias
`dX.Y`, where `X.Y` is the number of the example. For example, `d3.7` is the
`myeloma` data used in Example 3.7, and `d8.4` is the baseline cirrhosis data.
The aliases are ordinary data objects: `d3.7` works after `library(sta310r)`, and
`?d3.7` opens the help page of the data set. See
`vignette("datasets-by-exercise")`.

Note that 2 data sets are used in example 8.4 (hence no aliases used there). 

```{r}
library(sta310r)
dataset_by_exercise |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(chapter)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(chapter = paste(chapter, chapter_title, sep = ". ")) |>
  dplyr::select(chapter, example, alias, dataset, n_rows, n_variables) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "chapter", id = "datasets-by-example")
```

## Computer exercises

The course exercises are shipped as vignettes. The first exercise covers
censoring, the survivor and hazard functions, Kaplan–Meier, Nelson–Aalen and the
log-rank family:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
vignette("cs1-survival-data")
vignette("cs1-solutions")
```
